names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 26 mai, «Sfântul Apostol Carp».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Κάρπος ο Απόστολος από τους Εβδομήκοντα», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 26. мај ст. ст., „Свети апостол Карп“ — Свети is not a rank and апостол is the `apostle` this corpus puts in `types`; strip the two and the bare personal name is the whole of what the heading gives. **Measured**: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Карп», so this is the first folder to hold it, and the corpus keeps no other Carpus. The Greek form on this folder, «Κάρπος», and the Romanian «Carp» are the same bare name.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 26 mai — «Sfântul Apostol Carp»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 26ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Κάρπος ο Απόστολος από τους Εβδομήκοντα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 26 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar keeps «Sfântul Apostol Carp» on, with the same rank and the same place among the Seventy — and the Greek adds the same see argued two ways: «έγινε επίσκοπος στη Βάρνα της Θράκης (ο δε Σ. Ευστρατιάδης, αναφέρει Βέρροια της Θράκης)», Varna or Berroia of Thrace, the page naming Eustratiades for the second. **No `locations` object is proposed** on a see the source gives two names for. The page puts him in the reign of Nero, «(52 μ.Χ.)», which is a year inside a reign and not a year of his own, so the folder's empty `dates` is left empty. It rests his work at Troas on 2 Timothy 4,13, and says he died peacefully — he is therefore not the Carpus the corpus keeps as `carpus-of-thyatira`, a martyr with Papylus. Three hymns are added, the first of them the common of an apostle; the page's megalynarion and kathisma cannot be held by the schema's `kind` enum.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 08.06.2026 (26. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети апостол Карп“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, on the same menologion 26/5 the Romanian and Greek rows already carry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23 to 26 May is. **THIS BOOK BREAKS A TIE BETWEEN THE OTHER TWO, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE VALUE OF THE ROW.** doxologia has him **killed savagely and without mercy by the Jews who had not believed**; saint.gr says flatly **„He died peacefully, giving light by his example to many“**. The two accounts already on this folder contradict each other on whether he was martyred at all, and the folder holds `martyr` in `types` off the Romanian reading. **The Prologue is with doxologia**: „он је најзад пострадао од неверних Јевреја, и убијен био“ — he suffered at last from the unbelieving Jews and was killed. **So it is two books against one, and `martyr` stands where it was.** The contradiction is not resolved by a count and is left on the folder as a contradiction; what changes is that the reading which supports the stored type now has a second witness, and that is said rather than assumed. **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THE FOLDER STAYS UNDATED ON PURPOSE.** The existing source line records „the page gives no year, and none is recorded here“, saint.gr dates him only by the reign of Nero, and **the Prologue gives no year at all**. A reign is not a source for a year in this corpus, so the folder is left undated and that is now the answer of three calendars. **New here, and it is little but it is his character rather than his acts**: that Dionysius witnesses of him that he was **a man of unusually pure mind, of meekness and of guilelessness** — „човек необично чистог ума, кротости и незлобивости“ — which neither other page gives; and that **the Lord Jesus appeared to him in a vision with His angels**, where doxologia’s vision is the Lord alone, answering a prayer that two sinners be punished, with the words *Strike me instead*. **The two visions are not told as one and neither was made to swallow the other.** Everything else the entry gives, both other books already gave: one of the Seventy, follower and companion of Paul, set by him bishop of Beroea in Thrace, preaching in Crete, receiving Dionysius the Areopagite into his house, and Dionysius’s testimony that he never began the holy liturgy without a heavenly vision first. **`related` UNTOUCHED at `dionysius-the-areopagite`**, who is the only person in this entry with a folder whom the body puts in his story. **The apostle Paul takes no new row**: `paul-the-apostle` is in the corpus and the existing life already names him four times with no row and no exclusion, `related-floor.test.mjs` not matching the bare form, and **an ordination is not the kinship or the martyrdom that owes a row** — so nothing is added and nothing is quietly relied on. The unbelieving Jews are not persons. No `locations`, although Beroea, Thrace and Crete are all named. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the four hymns on this folder stay.

hymns.text: Apostole Sfinte Carp, roagă pe milostivul Dumnezeu, ca să dăruiască iertare de greşeli sufletelor noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Apostol Carp, unul din cei șaptezeci», Glasul 3

english.text: Holy apostle Carpus, entreat the merciful God to grant our souls forgiveness of our sins.

hymns.text: Ἀπόστολε Ἅγιε Κάρπε, πρέβευε τῷ ἐλεήμονι Θεῷ , ἵνα πταισμάτων ἄφεσιν, παράσχῃ ταῖς ψυχαῖς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, on the page of «Άγιος Κάρπος ο Απόστολος από τους Εβδομήκοντα» — the common of an apostle

english.text: Holy apostle Carpus, intercede with the merciful God that he may grant our souls forgiveness of our offences.

hymns.text: Θείας χάριτος, τῇ κοινωνίᾳ, ἐκοινώνησας, δεσμῶν τῷ Παύλῳ, θεομακάριστε Κάρπε Ἀπόστολε, καὶ κοινωνοὺς θείας δόξης ἀνέδειξας, τοὺς δεξαμένους τὸ φέγγος τῶν λόγων σου. Ὅθεν πρέσβευε, Χριστῷ τῷ Θεῷ πανεύφημε, δωρήσασθαι ἡμῖν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Θείας Πίστεως, on the page of «Άγιος Κάρπος ο Απόστολος από τους Εβδομήκοντα»

english.text: Sharing in the fellowship of divine grace, you shared Paul's bonds as well, Carpus, apostle blessed of God, and showed those who received the radiance of your words to be sharers of the divine glory. Therefore intercede with Christ God, all-praised one, that the great mercy may be given us.

hymns.text: Καρποφόρος πέφηνας, τῇ μυστικῇ γεωργίᾳ, ὡς κλεινὸς Ἀπόστολος, καὶ ὑπηρέτης τοῦ Λόγου· ὅθεν σου, ὁ τῶν ἀγώνων καρπὸς ὁ θεῖος, κάρπωμα, τερπνὸν προσήχθη τῷ Παντεπόπτῃ· ὃν ἱκέτευε ἀπαύστως, Κάρπε θεόφρον, ἐλεηθῆναι ἡμᾶς.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον, on the page of «Άγιος Κάρπος ο Απόστολος από τους Εβδομήκοντα»

english.text: You were shown fruitful in the mystical husbandry, a renowned apostle and a servant of the Word; and so the divine fruit of your labours was brought as a pleasing offering to him who beholds all things. Entreat him unceasingly, God-minded Carpus, that mercy may be shown us.
